chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Laythi narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani narrated to us. He said: Ya'qub ibn Yusuf ibn Ziyad narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Hammad narrated to us from 'Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from al-Husayn ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them all). He said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: I am the City of Wisdom — and that is Paradise — and you, O Ali, are its Gate. So how can the guided one be guided to Paradise, when one cannot be guided to it except through its Gate?

key_terms.الْحِكْمَة: Wisdom (hikma) — divine knowledge and guidance, here equated with Paradise
key_terms.الْمُهْتَدِي: The guided one — one who seeks or has received divine guidance
key_terms.بَابُهَا: Its gate — Ali's role as the gateway to the Prophet's wisdom and consequently to salvation
key_terms.مَدِينَةُ الْحِكْمَةِ: City of Wisdom — a title the Prophet gives himself, equating divine knowledge with access to Paradise

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet mean when he said 'I am the City of Wisdom and Ali is its Gate'?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a saying of the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) transmitted through a chain of Imams ending with Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS), in which the Prophet describes himself as the 'City of Wisdom' — and identifies that City with Paradise — and designates Imam Ali as its only Gate. The rhetorical question at the end underscores the theological point: just as entering a city requires its gate, attaining salvation and guidance requires the walayah (authority/guardianship) of Ali. This tradition was cited in debates about the Imamate, and the equation of hikma (wisdom) with jannah (Paradise) reflects the Shia understanding that true guidance is inseparable from the Ahlulbayt.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. Ahmad b. Ibrahim al-Laythi narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad al-Hamadani narrated to us. He said: Ya`qub b. Yusuf b. Ziyad narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Hammad narrated to us from `Amr b. Shimr from Jabir from Abi Ja`far al-Baqir from `Ali b. al-Husayn from al-Husayn b. `Ali from `Ali b. Abi Talib (as). He said:
The Messenger of Allah (s) said: I am the City of Wisdom – and that is Paradise – and you, `Ali, are its Gate. So, how can a guided one be guided to Paradise without being guided to it by its Gate?
